title: How To Handle A Class That Tests You Right From The Get-Go rom-the-get-go/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin describes the disheartening scenario of a class that begins misbehaving almost immediately after the teacher introduces a classroom management plan, and reassures teachers this doesn't doom the year. His prescribed first response is to do nothing: stop, breathe, and observe rather than reacting or rushing to enforce consequences, which can incite pushback. If students settle on their own, the teacher should calmly re-teach the plan with more conviction, boldness, and detail than before, modeling and role-playing consequences so nothing is left to chance. If misbehavior recurs days later, he advises scrapping the planned lesson and re-teaching the management plan again, repeating as many times as necessary until students genuinely internalize it. He frames the willingness to project confidence — even faked, if needed — as an act of courage central to winning over a difficult class.
points: Being tested right after introducing a management plan is common and not predictive of a bad year.
First response to early testing should be to wait, breathe, and observe rather than immediately enforcing consequences.
Re-teach the classroom management plan with greater boldness, detail, and conviction than the first time.
If misbehavior recurs, cancel the planned lesson and re-teach the plan again — repeat as many times as it takes.
Projecting confidence, even when faked, is described as a form of courage necessary to win over a tough class.
quotes: It’s disheartening—and only natural to feel as if you did something wrong.
So if it happens to you, there is no need to panic. In fact, your first response should be to do absolutely nothing.
Just wait. Breathe. Observe. Smile inwardly—because you’re going to fix it.
Most teachers will try to enforce consequences as fast as they can, but this is a mistake with a large group of misbehaving students because it risks inciting aggressive and disrespectful pushback.

Exceptional classroom management, especially with a tough class, takes courage . And if you’re not feeling confident, if your heart is beating out of your chest and your palms are sweaty, then fake it .
Teach it until they “get it.” Teach it until they know that rebelling is futile.
